names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Βίκτωρ, Ζωτικός, Ακίνδυνος, Καισάριος, Σεβηριανός, Χριστόφορος, Ζήνων, Θεωνάς και Αντωνίνος», with the rank word left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Ζωτικός (; - 303)».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 18 April, „Св. муч. Виктор, Зотик, Зинон, Акиндин и Северијан.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and муч. left off, which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. One rank word stands over all five names and belongs to none of them, and the heading gives no epithet, no city and no year to any of them, so the bare forename is the whole of what the source gives; the day in this folder's display name is the corpus's own way of telling the company's members from their namesakes and is not part of any source's name. `zoticus-of-nicomedia` already holds this same bare form in Serbian and in Russian both; the fold is recorded as deliberate in the run's findings.

death.note: saint.gr heads each of the nine «(; - 303)» and closes its account of them «Ήταν το έτος 303 μ.Χ.»; no year of birth is printed.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ής Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Βίκτωρ, Ζωτικός, Ακίνδυνος, Καισάριος, Σεβηριανός, Χριστόφορος, Ζήνων, Θεωνάς και Αντωνίνος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Nine people are named and enumerated on the page, and this corpus makes one folder for each. The page divides them: Victor, Acindynus, Zoticus, Zeno and Severian confessed when they saw [George the Trophy-bearer](/saints/george-the-trophy-bearer) left unhurt on the wheel and were beheaded at once, while Christopher, Theonas, Caesarius and Antoninus were the king's own guards and confessed when they saw George raise a dead man by prayer. It heads each of the nine «(; - 303)» and closes «Ήταν το έτος 303 μ.Χ.», so the death year is taken and no year of birth. It sets them all in the reign of Diocletian, which it dates 284 to 305. The corpus's other bearers of these names — Acindynus and Severian of Nicomedia on 22 August, Christopher on 9 May, Theonas of Thessalonica on 4 April, Victor of Chalcedon on 16 September and the rest — are other men on other days, and none of their lives names George. The page prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.05.2026 (18. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Виктор, Зотик, Зинон, Акиндин и Северијан.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, an enumerated company of five, so one row each. **The Prologue keeps them on the Julian 18 April where saint.gr keeps them on 20 April**, and one row per church means the Greek row kept its day and nothing moved. **The identification is a reading and is stated as one**: the entry says all five were tortured in the time of the emperor Diocletian, that they were pagans until they saw the torments of George the Great Martyr, and that seeing those torments, his courage and the many wonders that appeared then they received the Christian faith, for which they soon suffered and were crowned. saint.gr's company of nine on 20 April is the same account — nine pagans converted at George's trial, dead 303 — and the Prologue's five names are five of those nine, spelling for spelling. **The other four the Greek page names — Christopher, Theonas, Caesarius and Antoninus — are not in this heading and took no row.** No date was added and none changed: the entry names Diocletian and prints no year, where the folder already holds saint.gr's 303, so there was nothing to add and nothing to displace. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
